It asks route.mjs for the path, base, key name and provider id instead of hardcoding DashScope and its own map, the router's answer being byte-identical at base and HEAD with only a providerModel field added, and it counts the key its own call passes. A missing secret exits 0 with a reason naming the key and the path. The packet arrives on stdin. Five mutations were driven red by the control plane on the corrected branch, each with a property-level message: the child's OPENAI_BASE_URL, its OPENAI_API_KEY, its OPENAI_MODEL, an argv element carrying the packet, and watch printing idle while a lane is issued. F35 makes the alumni scan open the TRAPS file it already detects, so a lesson a child wrote in prose stops reaching the parent only when a person reads it, which is T71; it must split rows that name a check from rows that do not, emit only the former as candidate intakes, and count the rest, because an intake without a check is refused and a refused intake is noise the owner learns to skip. Nine ledger rows and one decision row were dated from this session's local clock, 2026-09-21 in UTC+8, while UTC had not yet reached that day: date -u printed 2026-09-20 22:34 while date printed 2026-09-21 06:34. F35 returned at 3c1dd95 and the review says CORRECTIONS NEEDED on the boundary the envelope told it to look hardest at. splitCheck takes the first case-insensitive match of check is or check colon, so ordinary prose beats the real directive: a row reading Confirm the box, then lowercase check is ticked before merge, then the real Check is node factory/tools/kitCheck.mjs --self-test, emits a rule of Confirm the box Confirm the box and a check of ticked before merge, always, with the real directive glued to the end. Driven at the objects through alumni.mjs intakes on a fixture tree, and that candidate clears the twelve-character floor and passes intake.mjs unedited, which is worse than being held because the owner acts on it. The same root cause has an inverse the printed list cannot distinguish: a false hit early in a row pushes the rule under its floor and a row with a good check is held as if it had none. Correction 1 makes the match case-sensitive and last-wins, with a fixture for each half. It also guards the module's dispatch, because node -e importing alumni.mjs prints the whole check pack, which is T14 latent and the same hazard F36 fixed in packet.mjs.
